## Summary

I implemented the disposable-domain email blocklist in the owner-creation endpoint (`POST /api/owners`), handled by `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`.

Changes in `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`:

1. **Blocklist constant** — a `Set<String> DISPOSABLE_EMAIL_DOMAINS` containing `mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, `guerrillamail.com`.
2. **Rejection check** — in `addOwner`, alongside the other 400-level validations, the request is rejected with `400 BAD_REQUEST` when the owner's email domain is on the blocklist.
3. **Helper `isDisposableEmailDomain`** — extracts the domain (part after the last `@`), normalizes it (trim + lowercase, matching the app's existing email-normalization idiom), and checks membership. Null/malformed emails pass through (no domain to block), so owners without an email are unaffected.

The check sits before persistence and before the duplicate/quota logic, so disposable-domain owners are rejected cleanly without side effects.

Null/malformed emails pass through (no domain to block), so owners without an email are unaffected.

The check sits before persistence and before the duplicate/quota logic, so disposable-domain owners are rejected cleanly without side effects.
